subcategory: Unravel the natural splendor of Andhra Pradesh in Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary, a serene haven teeming with diverse flora and fauna.

subcategory: India's Second Largest Underground Karst Cave System (3.2 Km)
description: Formed over tens of thousands of years by the subterranean flow of the Chitravati River, the second largest and longest cave system in the Indian subcontinent, descending to depths of 150 feet (Pataalaganga) with caverns, stalactites, stalagmites, and Buddhist relics.

hidden_gem_reason: An extraordinary natural underground karst labyrinth extending deep beneath the Deccan plains, fully equipped with boardwalks and cool ventilation systems.

distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 30 km from Tadipatri / 105 km from Kurnool
notes: AP Tourism has installed powerful oxygen blowers and illumination throughout the accessible tourist route.

distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 180 km from Kurnool / 215 km from Hyderabad

subcategory: India's Largest Tiger Reserve & Deep Eastern Ghats

why_visit: Experience thrilling forest safari drives through wild deciduous valleys, spot roaming spotted deer and sambar, and discover ancient Chenchu tribal forest culture.
hidden_gem_reason: One of India's most expansive and wildest tiger conservation landscapes, rugged and untouched.

distance_from_nearest_famous_place: Flanking Srisailam highway across Nandyal and Palnadu

subcategory: Colossal Krishna River Hydroelectric Gorge Dam

activities: Dam Viewing; Gorge Photography; Srisailam Ropeway Ride; Krishna River Boating
notes: Supplies power and irrigation to both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; scenic ghat road descent.

subcategory: 1530 CE Vijayanagara Engineering Wonder with Monolithic Nandi & Hanging Pillar
description: Constructed in 1530 CE by Virupanna Nayaka atop the Kurma Saila (tortoise-shaped hill), an architectural masterpiece renowned for its mysterious Hanging Pillar that does not touch the ground, Asia's largest single-stone monolithic Nandi bull, and ceiling frescoes.

activities: Hanging Pillar Inspection; Monolithic Nandi Photography; Vijayanagara Mural Study; 7-Hooded Snake Linga Viewing

notes: According to legend, this is where Lord Rama found the wounded Jatayu and uttered 'Le Pakshi' ('Rise, bird').
